tool_schemas.name: rollback
tool_schemas.description: Roll a service back to a previously released version in all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: deploy
tool_schemas.description: Deploy a version of a service to all production regions.

tool_schemas.description: Open an incident; this pages the on-call engineer.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. A request repeated with the same key is never executed again: the service returns the original outcome. Reuse the key when retrying the same request.

args.summary: checkout-api failed health checks after deploy of v2.3.1 (error rate 18%, service unhealthy). Per runbook, rolled back all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) to the most recent previously healthy release, v2.3.0. First rollback attempt partially failed (orchestrator error halted rollout after us-east only); a retry completed the rollout to the remaining regions. Post-rollback: all regions on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate 0.2%. Root cause of v2.3.1 failure still under investigation; recommend the owning team investigate before any redeploy of v2.3.1.
args.title: checkout-api outage after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0

trace.final:
All done. Here's a summary:

**Actions taken:**
1. **Reviewed deployment history** — found v2.3.1 was the latest production deploy and unhealthy; v2.3.0 was the most recent healthy release.
2. **Rolled back checkout-api to v2.3.0 in all regions.** The first attempt failed partway (orchestrator error, only us-east completed), leaving us-west and eu-west still on broken v2.3.1. A retry completed the rollout successfully.
3. **Verified recovery** — all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) now on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate down from 18% to 0.2%.
4. **Opened SEV2 incident INC-0001** (first creation attempt timed out; retried safely with an idempotency key), and the on-call engineer has been paged. The incident documents the outage, the partial-failure hiccup during rollback, and notes that root cause of the v2.3.1 failure still needs investigation before redeploy.
